steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Lanternix on this image exposes /app/bin/lanternix. That mill is a native ELF Go program; the file begins with 7fELF. A script or interpreter at that path is not enough. Cast and readout usage plus JSON field rules live in /app/notes/ROUTE.txt and /app/notes/GRAMMAR.txt. Repair the Go pipeline modules named in /app/notes/ROUTE.txt. Source edits under /app are required. Hand-written readout JSON is not enough.

On this image lanternix cast exits 0. readout of /app/lamps/flash9c.lamp exits 2 and does not write /app/glowbank/readout.json. A correct mill's readout of that lamp must carry the lamp file values as strings in readout.json slots using the names from its card. Recipe lamps flash9c, held, warm, and beam must decode. Generated unit packages under /app/packbay/units must be imported by /app/packbay/reg.go.

A recipe card whose id the mill does not carry makes readout exit non-zero and must not replace a success readout.json. A lamp whose code is absent from /app/cardwell still reports void and exits non-zero. The verifier reruns readout only.

Analysis: The defects are visible: packbay.Pull only recognizes two IDs; reg.go imports only unita/unitb; generated slot names preserve unwanted whitespace; Spin hard-codes only two imports; and readout boots the registry before Pull, so any loading done by Pull would occur too late for oxbind's snapshot. Cast now exits 2, likely because its generator wrote malformed Go source: unitSource appears to insert a literal newline inside a quoted Go string. We need recover exact, untruncated source and inspect files as they exist after the failed cast.
Plan: Print complete numbered milldesk sources and current generated files, then run gofmt/go test to expose syntax/build errors. Based on that, replace the broken parser/generator/registry logic with robust implementations, rebuild via the ship target, run cast, and test all success and failure semantics.

Analysis: The Go tool exists outside the shell PATH (the source itself expects /usr/local/go/bin). Current generated files remain syntactically valid, but cast hard-codes only two unit imports and therefore rebuilds an incomplete mill. Card slot parsing fails to trim each comma-separated name, causing incorrect JSON keys. Readout snapshots the store before loading units. The failure behavior ordering is otherwise useful: unsupported cards are checked before writing, while an unknown lamp code can produce void.
Plan: Rewrite the affected pipeline modules: make Pull load the full generated registry, load before oxbind.Boot in readout, trim card slot names, propagate JSON write errors, and make cast discover/import every generated unit directory. Generate valid quoted Go source, format generated files, then build the native binary using the explicit Go path. Run cast and comprehensive tests for all recipe lamps, alien void behavior, preservation of successful JSON when an unsupported ghost card exists, generated imports, and ELF magic.

root@694b6d4b8f50:/app# sed -n '1,220p' milldesk/spin.go; printf '\n--- Makefile bytes/text ---\n'; cat -A milldesk/Makefile
package main

import (
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "os/exec"
        "path/filepath"
        "sort"
        "strconv"
        "strings"
)

func Spin() int {
        cards, err := loadCards("/app/cardwell")
        if err != nil {
                return 2
        }
        if err := writeUnits(cards); err != nil {
                return 2
        }
        units, err := unitDirs("/app/packbay/units")
        if err != nil {
                return 2
        }
        if err := writeFill(units); err != nil {
                return 2
        }
        cmd := exec.Command("/usr/local/go/bin/go", "build", "-o", "/app/bin/lanternix.next", "loft.local/lanternix/milldesk")
        cmd.Dir = "/app"
        cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
                "GOPROXY=off",
                "GOFLAGS=-mod=mod",
                "GOCACHE=/tmp/gocache-lanternix",
        )
        if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
                return 2
        }
        if err := os.Rename("/app/bin/lanternix.next", "/app/bin/lanternix"); err != nil {
                return 2
        }
        return 0
}

func writeUnits(cards []card) error {
        roots := map[string]string{
                "LAN_WARM_01":  "unita",
                "LAN_BEAM_44":  "unitb",
                "LAN_FLASH_9C": "unitc",
                "LAN_GLOW_2B":  "unitd",
        }
        for _, c := range cards {
                dir, ok := roots[c.id]
                if !ok {
                        continue
                }
                p := filepath.Join("/app/packbay/units", dir, "pack.go")
                if err := os.WriteFile(p, []byte(unitSource(dir, c.id, c.slots)), 0o644); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
        }
        return nil
}

func unitSource(pkg, id string, slots []string) string {
        quoted := make([]string, 0, len(slots))
        for _, slot := range slots {
                quoted = append(quoted, strconv.Quote(strings.TrimSpace(slot)))
        }
        return fmt.Sprintf("package %s\n\nimport \\\"loft.local/lanternix/packbay/store\\\"\n\nfunc Load() {\n\\tstore.Offer(%s, store.Spec{Slots: []string{%s}}
)\n}\n", pkg, strconv.Quote(id), strings.Join(quoted, ", "))
}

func unitDirs(root string) ([]string, error) {
        entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        var units []string
        for _, entry := range entries {
                if entry.IsDir() {
                        units = append(units, entry.Name())
                }
        }
        sort.Strings(units)
        return units, nil
}

func writeFill(units []string) error {
        var b strings.Builder
        b.WriteString("package packbay\n\nimport (\n")
        for i, unit := range units {
                fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\\tu%d %s\n", i, strconv.Quote("loft.local/lanternix/packbay/units/"+unit))
        }
        b.WriteString(")\n\nfunc Fill() {\n")
        for i := range units {
                fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\\tu%d.Load()\n", i)
        }
        b.WriteString("}\n")
        return os.WriteFile("/app/packbay/reg.go", []byte(b.String()), 0o644)
}
